newsitem.title: USA: Digital wireless seen boosting telcom Q1 sales.
newsitem.headline: Digital wireless seen boosting telcom Q1 sales.

text.p: Brisk sales of digital wireless phone networks should bolster earnings for two giant telecommunications equipment makers during the seasonally weak first quarter and carry the momentum throughout the rest of the year, industry analysts say.

The new technology offered by Lucent Technologies Inc and Northern Telecom Ltd has met strong demand among phone operators and other companies who see it as the successor to the older analog cellular service.
Neil Danzger of Morgan Stanley said he expected Nortel's first-quarter earnings to surpass First Call's consensus among analysts by $0.01 a share at $0.38.
"Like Lucent, Northern should provide an upside surprise given what we expect will be a continuing ramp in wireless infrastructure rollout," he said in a report.
Robert Wilkes of Brown Brothers Harriman also foresaw good figures from Nortel.
"I see broad strength in most of its products with the possible exception of central office switching," he said, explaining how sales for the switches had slowed down since the fourth quarter.

Wilkes said the company's Synchronous Optical Network (SONET) rings, which improve the reliability of transmission over fibre optic cables, were bound to meet good demand in the United States during the rest of 1997.
Theodosopoulos at UBS said he expected Nortel to surpass First Call's consensus, projecting a profit of $0.38 a share against $0.32 for the same period a year ago.
Nortel, which is to release its earnings on April 22, has projected 1997 sales to grow between 15 percent and 20 percent and earnings even faster.

Lucent has already given an earnings forecast for the first three months of the year, seeing second-quarter earnings between $0.09 a share and $0.10 a share. It cited cost reduction, higher revenues from wireless networks, and strong sales in software and wireless communications systems.
First Call had a consensus of $0.07 a share for the company, which had a $0.16 loss for the same period last year.
Michael Schmidt at CS First Boston said he expected Lucent to follow the industry's 10-percent growth rate for the rest of the year, given its array of products and size.

"There are few companies that can deliver a large-scale, fully-functioning network that Lucent can," he said, referring to how it delivered half the network for Sprint on time. FIRST CALL ESTIMATES VS REPORTED YEAR AGO COMPANY (ALL IN DLRS) Q2 YR AGO RESULTS DATE
